title: Genetic in vivo engineering of human T lymphocytes in mouse models
protocol: Seed 2x10^7 cells in 18 ml DMEM (10% FBS, 2 mM L-glutamine) per 15 cm cell culture plate.
Dilute cells to a concentration of 2x10^6 cells/ml.
Add 10 ml of the cell suspension to each plate.
Handle plates carefully to avoid contaminations.
Evenly spread the cells on the plates by tilting the plate back and forth and from left to right after seeding.
Observe cells under the microscope to check for their condition and possible contaminations.
Replace medium in all dishes by 12 ml DMEM containing 15% FBS and 2 mM L-glutamine.
Separately prepare the DNA Mix and PEI Mix required for transfection in conical-bottom, sterile polypropylene tubes.
Prepare DNA Mix in a 250 ml tube by combining 92 ml DMEM with 606.9 μg pS-CD19.CAR-W and 577.8 μg pCMV-dR8.91.
Add 35.9 μg of pCAGGS-NiV-GcΔ34-αCD8opt and 179.5 μg pCAGGS-NiV-FcΔ22 for CD8-LV production or 53.9 μg of pCG-Hmut-CD4.DARPin29.2 and 161.5 μg of pCG-FcΔ30 for CD4-LV production.
Prepare PEI Mix in another 250 ml tube by combining 5.6 ml PEI with 88 ml DMEM without supplements.
Thoroughly mix PEI-Mix by vortexing for 30 seconds.
Thoroughly mix DNA-Mix by vortexing for 30 seconds.
Add PEI-Mix to DNA-Mix and vortex again for 30 seconds.
Incubate the mixture for 20-30 minutes at room temperature.
Pipette 4.6 ml of the transfection mix to each plate using a 10-ml pipette.
Tilt the plates carefully to disperse the medium evenly.
Return the dishes to the tissue culture incubator.
Incubate them overnight at 37°C with a humidified atmosphere containing 5% CO₂.
Stack the dishes horizontally to ensure cells are completely covered with medium at all times.
Gently aspirate the medium from the cells.
Add 18 ml of DMEM (10% FBS, 2 mM L-glutamine) to the cells.
Incubate the plates in a tissue culture incubator at 37°C for 24 hours.
Filter the cell supernatant through a 0.45 µm Bottle Top Filter placed on a 500 ml storage bottle.
Keep the supernatant on ice after filtration.
Store at least one aliquot of the unconcentrated filtered cell culture supernatant at -80°C or 4°C for titration the next day.
Distribute the filtered supernatant to four 250 ml conical centrifuge tubes.
Aspirate 14 ml of the 20% sucrose solution with a 10-ml pipette.
Insert the pipette to the bottom of one centrifuge tube containing the filtered supernatant and slowly underlay with 9 ml of the sucrose solution.
Stop expelling the solution when it hits the 5 ml mark on the pipette.
Discard the rest of the solution and use a new pipette for each subsequent tube.
Balance the tubes by adding PBS without Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺ until the weight difference is below 0.1 g.
Centrifuge for 24 hours at 4°C (4500×g; acceleration: 6; deceleration: 6) in a benchtop centrifuge.
Set the centrifuge on “Hold” for at least 24 hours to ensure it does not finish before proceeding.
Fill Open-Top Thinwall polypropylene tubes to maximum capacity with supernatant if using ultracentrifugation.
If necessary, fill up the supernatant to exactly 30 ml with PBS w/o Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺ before adding 5 ml sucrose solution for ultracentrifugation.
Aspirate supernatant with a 10 ml pipette and filter it through a 0.45 μm syringe filter if production is downscaled to less than 10 plates per vector.
Transfer filtered supernatant of two culture plates into a 50 ml centrifuge tube for concentration in cases where production is downscaled.
Underlay the filtered supernatant with 4.5 ml 20% sucrose by aspirating 7.5 ml of sucrose solution and stopping to expel when it hits the 3 ml mark on the pipette.
Carefully remove the tubes from the centrifuge.
Discard the supernatant quickly but carefully to avoid bubbles.
Leave the tube upside down for 5 minutes on a rack lined with paper towels.
Wipe the tubes with fresh paper towels without touching the pellet.
Add 600-1000 µl PBS w/o Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺ to each pellet without touching it.
Let the pellet resuspend for 30 minutes by placing the tubes on ice on a plate shaker.
Pipette up and down 80 times with an electronic pipette.
Pool the liquids from all resuspended pellets in one conical tube.
Aliquot the vector stock in low binding tubes in volumes of 15-200 µl.
Store the vectors at -80°C.
Dilute lentiviral vectors 1:1,000 - 1:10,000 in PBS without Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺ (typically 1:3,000) for measurement via NTA with Nanosight NS300.
Incubate CD8+/CD4+ cells with 5 µl vector stock per 4x10^4 cells in 96-well plates.
Seed cells in 100 μl RPMI medium (10% FBS, 2 mM L-glutamine) for incubation.
Add vector stock diluted in 100 μl medium to get a final volume of 200 μl per well.
Determine the percentage of transduced cells via flow cytometry three or four days later using appropriate antibodies.
Coat a 24-well plate with 500 μl of 1 μg/ml anti-human CD3 mAb.
Incubate the coated plate for 2 hours at 37°C or overnight at 4°C.
Remove the medium and replace it with 2% BSA in PBS without Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺.
Incubate for 30 minutes at 37°C.
Wash the plate twice with PBS without Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺.
Seed 2x10⁶ PBMC in 2 ml T Cell medium (TCM) supplemented with 3 μg/ml anti-human CD28 mAb and 50 U/ml IL-2.
Incubate for 72 hours at 37°C, 5% CO₂, and 90% humidity.
Seed 0.4-1x10⁵ activated PBMC in a volume of 100 μl TCM + 50 U/ml IL-2 per well in a 96-well plate.
Transduce the cells with 5 μl vector stock diluted in 100 μl medium per well.
Perform spinfection at 850×g (acceleration: 7, deceleration: 7) for 90 minutes in a preheated centrifuge at 32°C.
Add 100 μl TCM into each well after spinfection.
Incubate the cells at 37°C, 5% CO₂, and 90% humidity.
Cultivate the transduced cells for 4-7 days before determining the number of transduced cells via flow cytometry with corresponding antibodies.
Weigh each NSG mouse and calculate the precise volume of busulfex to apply a dose of 20 mg/kg per mouse.
Pre-dilute the stock solution of busulfex (6 mg/ml) with sterile PBS just before injection if necessary.
Carefully remove the animal from the cage and restrain it gently in the head-down position.
Insert the needle with the bevel facing “up” into the lower right quadrant of the abdomen towards the head at a 30-40° angle to the horizontal line.
Inject the appropriate volume of busulfex solution intra-peritoneally in a steady, fluid motion.
Warm up 30 ml CellGro medium in a 37°C water bath.
Take cells from the liquid nitrogen tank and thaw them in the water bath at 37°C for 1-2 min.
Transfer CD34+ cells very quickly to a prewarmed 50 ml tube containing 30 ml CellGro medium.
Spin the tube at 300×g for 10 min at room temperature.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend cells in 2 ml CellGro medium.
Count the cells using a hemocytometer after trypan blue staining.
Spin down the cell suspension at 300×g for 10 min at 4°C and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 1 ml of complete CellGro medium at a density of 1-10^6 living cells/ml and seed in a 24-well plate.
Incubate cells at 37°C, 5% CO₂, 20% O₂ overnight (16 h to 24 h).
Collect cells in 1.5 ml tubes prior to transplantation.
Count cells using a hemocytometer after trypan blue staining.
Spin down CD34+ HSPCs at 300×g for 10 min at RT and resuspend them with sterile PBS w/o Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺ to 0.7x10⁵ - 2x10⁵ cells per 35 μl total volume for each mouse to be injected.
Take the cells from Step 34 to the animal facility (experimental area).
Mix the cells immediately prior to injection by pipetting up and down.
Load the syringe (29-gauge needles, 0.3 to 0.5 ml insulin syringes) with cell suspension at a volume of 30 μl per mouse.
Mice should be anaesthetised before needle placement in the retro-bulbar space.
Perform anaesthesia using a decontaminated induction box with 3.5% isoflurane enriched air until the mouse becomes non-responsive, recumbent, and exhibits a slower, even respiratory pattern.
Maintain anaesthesia using a nose cone releasing 1-2% isoflurane enriched air.
Place the anaesthetized mouse on a sterile compress with its belly facing up on the surface of the laminar flow.
Protrude the right eyeball from the eye socket by applying gentle pressure to the skin at the dorsal and ventral part of the eye.
Introduce the needle bevel down at an angle of approximately 30° into the medial canthus.
Inject the cell suspension slowly and smoothly.
Remove the needle slowly and smoothly once the injection is complete.
Place mice back into the cage for recovery after injection.
Handle NSG mice under a laminar flow hood.
Provide sterile food and water to NSG mice.
Keep NSG mice in sterile cages.
Ensure strict handling protocols are followed to prevent opportunistic infections in NSG mice.
Apply a drop of tetracaine 5 min prior to sampling blood from the eye.
Perform retro-orbital blood sampling by penetrating the retro-orbital sinus in mice with a sterile hematocrit capillary tube or Pasteur pipette.
Take approximately 100 µl blood per mouse in 1.5-ml sterile microcentrifuge tubes containing 20 µl of CPD for plasma collection and gDNA analysis.
Immediately pipette 50 µl in a new tube containing 20 µl of CPD and place on ice for FACS staining.
Samples can be kept on ice for up to 12 hours.
Add 50-100 µl PBS without Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺ to the blood (1:1 ratio).
Transfer 50 µl of 2x-diluted blood into 5 ml FACS tubes containing 50 µl of FACS Wash Buffer supplemented with the antibody cocktail.
Incubate for 30 min at 4°C in the dark.
Add 500 µl FACS Wash Buffer.
Centrifuge at 300×g for 10 min at 4°C.
Discard supernatant by inverting tube and gently tapping on paper towel to remove remaining drop of supernatant.
Add 700 µl of 1X RBC lysis buffer for 10 min at room temperature (dark).
Centrifuge at 300×g for 10 min at 4°C, discard supernatant and add 3-4 ml FACS Wash Buffer.
Spin the cells again at 300×g for 10 min at 4°C and remove supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 100-200 μl FACS Fixation Buffer.
Keep the cells in FACS tubes and then analyse via MACS Quant measurement.
Gate white blood cells by granularity and size (FSC vs. SSC).
Evaluate gated cells for hCD45 (negative for mCD45) combined with hCD3, hCD19, or hCD14 using flow cytometry analysis.
Determine the human immune reconstitution by calculating the percentage of human CD45 cells divided by the total percentage of both human and murine CD45 cells.
Resuspend human IL7 according to manufacturer’s protocol.
Prepare a working solution at 2 μg/ml in sterile PBS without Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺.
Inject 100 μl of the working solution of huIL7 (200 ng) via the sub-cutaneous route.
Restrain the animal by grasping the skin along its back.
Insert the needle at the base of the skin fold between thumb and finger.
Administer IL7 in a steady, fluent motion with a 29G 0.5 ml syringe.
Inject a single dose of 2×10^11 LV particles i.v. using the same procedure as for human CD34+ cell injection.
Monitor mice every 3-4 days and euthanize them at the chosen time point after LV injection or when clinical endpoints are reached.
Anesthetize the mice by i.p. administration of ketamine and xylazine.
Collect more than 500 μl of blood in a 1.5 ml tube containing 100 μl CPD via retro-orbital blood sampling or intracardiac puncture.
Perform cervical dislocation.
Collect mouse tissues (spleen, lymph nodes, liver and others) in FACS Wash Buffer and keep them on ice immediately.
Fix the tissue in formalin 4% for 24 hours and wash in 70% ethanol.
Keep the organs in alcohol until paraffin-embedded slices are prepared from the fixed tissues.
Centrifuge blood at 300×g for 5 min at room temperature.
Transfer the upper phase to a 1.5 ml tube and centrifuge at 14,000×g for 5 min at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to a fresh 1.5 ml tube and store at -80°C.
Wash the remaining blood cells with 1 ml PBS without Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺ and centrifuge at 300×g for 5 min at 4°C.
Add 700 μl of 1X RBC lysis buffer for 10 min at room temperature (dark).
Perform the washing step as indicated in step 73.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 ml PBS without Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺ and count cells with trypan blue solution.
Place a 40 μm cell strainer on top of a 50 ml Falcon tube.
Put the spleen on the filter and use the plunger base of a syringe to mash the spleen while pouring PBS without Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺ through the strainer until the spleen is completely dissociated.
Centrifuge at 300×g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Discard supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 3 ml of PBS without Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺.
Put 2 ml of Lymphoprep solution in a 15 ml tube.
Slowly add 3 ml of cell suspension on top of the Lymphoprep solution.
Gently pipette the cells to avoid mixing the two phases.
Centrifuge at 850×g for 20 minutes at 20°C (acceleration: 1; deceleration: 0).
Carefully aspirate the upper phase, leaving 2-3 ml above the ring of mononuclear cells.
Carefully aspirate the ring of mononuclear cells with a 10 ml pipette and put into a new 50 ml tube.
Fill up the tube with PBS without Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺.
Spin at 300×g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend the pellet with 5-10 ml of PBS without Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺ to reach a concentration of 1-5x10⁶ cells/ml.
Count cells using trypan blue solution.

Alternatively, resuspend the cell pellet with 1 ml RBC lysis buffer and incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature. Then dilute the lysis buffer by adding 5 ml PBS without Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺ before centrifugation.

Use the single-cell suspension from spleen for DNA extraction and flow cytometry analysis. Place 1x10⁶ cells in a FACS tube and 2x10⁶ cells in a 1.5 ml tube for qPCR. Freeze any remaining cells at -80°C in freezing medium.
Place the femur into a 10 cm dish for mononuclear cell isolation from bone marrow.
(Note: The tibia can also be processed using this procedure.)
Remove the muscles and residual tissue surrounding the femur with sterile forceps and scissors.
Cut the femurs at both ends with sharp sterile scissors.

Flush the bone marrow onto a 40 µm nylon cell strainer placed in a 50 ml Falcon conical tube using a 23- or 25-gauge needle and a 10 cc syringe filled with ice-cold PBS without Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺ until the flow through turns transparent.
Dissociate the bone marrow through the cell strainer with a 5 ml plunger.
Wash the strainer with PBS without Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺.
Centrifuge cells at 300×g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet with 2 ml PBS without Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺.
Count bone marrow cells with a hemocytometer containing trypan blue.
Prepare single cell suspensions from spleen, bone marrow, and blood from each mouse.
Count cells and place 1x10^6 cells from each organ into separate micronics.
Wash cells twice with 500 μl FACS Wash Buffer.
Pellet cells at 400×g for 5 min at 4°C.
Resuspend cell pellet in blocking solution and incubate for 10 min at 4°C.
Add 50 μl of prepared antibody mixture or isotype control mixture to the respective well.
Incubate for 30 min in the dark at 4°C.
Wash cells with 500 μl FACS Wash Buffer.
Centrifuge at 400×g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant carefully.
Repeat the washing procedure.
Add 100 μl of viability dye to each well.
Incubate in the dark at 4°C for 20 min.
Perform the washing step as indicated previously.
Add 100 μl of FACS Fixation Buffer.
Resuspend the pellet.
Proceed to sample acquisition by flow cytometry.
Analyze samples using FlowJo software.
Enrich 2×10^6 cells from bone marrow or spleen for CD4+ and CD8+ cell population according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Freeze enriched cells at -80°C as a pellet for further analysis.
Isolate high-molecular weight genomic DNA from the enriched cells using the DNeasy kit.
Elute DNA with 200 μl of elution buffer.
Determine DNA concentration using Nanodrop.
Transfer 15 μl of reaction mix into the wells of a 96-well PCR plate.
Add 10 μl of sample containing 100 ng of DNA to the plate without mixing to achieve a total volume of 25 μl.
As a control, transfer 10 μl of serial dilutions (from 1x10^6 – 1x10^0 molecules/μl) to the plate containing the reaction mix.
Add 10 μl of DNase and RNase-free water as a negative control.
Seal the plate.
Centrifuge the plate at 20×g for 1 min at 4°C to mix samples with reaction mix.
Perform qPCR using the LightCycler 480 Instrument II (5 min at 95°C, 45 cycles of 10 sec at 95°C and 40 sec at 60°C).
